summary: Sensho Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University (~1962–1970). He later served as a professor at Otani University from around 1986 to 2014.

Sensho Murakami (1851–1929) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Toyo University. He held posts at Toyo University (~1887–1900), Tokyo Imperial University (~1899–1917), University of Tokyo (1916–1922), Otani University (~1926–1928), and Sendan-Rin School.

Seok-hyeong Kim is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University. He held posts as a part-time lecturer at Seoul National University (1945) and as a professor at Dongguk University.

Seong-Uk Kim specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied from around 2007 to 2013 under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr. and committee members William M. Bodiford and Richard von Glahn.

Sergey Oldenburg (1863–1934), an Indologist and Central Asian scholar, studied under Ivan Minayev at St. Petersburg University. He taught at Saint Petersburg State University (~1889–1899) and held posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences, Asiatic Museum, and Institute of Oriental Studies.

Serinity Young (d. 2020) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology who completed her Ph.D. at Columbia University under Alex Wayman. She held posts at the American Museum of Natural History and Southern Methodist University.

Seung-yeon Lee specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She earned her doctorate under Sang-hae Lee at Sungkyunkwan University, where she later held a post, and also held a position at the Gyeonggi Cultural Foundation.

Buddhist studies scholar Seunghak Koh earned an MA at Seoul National University and a PhD at UCLA (~2005–2011) under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He later served as an appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Seán McLoughlin is a scholar in religious studies and Indology who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Manchester (~1993–1997). In ~1999, he became a Lecturer in South Asian, Islamic and Religious Studies at the University of Leeds.

Shailendra Bhandare works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts at the British Museum and Fitzwilliam Museum, and around 2002 became Assistant Keeper at the Ashmolean Museum and a Fellow at St Cross College, Oxford.
Shan Shan Zhao is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at McMaster University (~2017–2019) under supervisor James A. Benn, also studying under Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.
Shane McCausland is a sinologist and art historian who studied at Princeton University (1996–2000). He took up a post at SOAS University of London in 2009.
Shanshan Jia is an Indology scholar who conducted doctoral studies at the University of Hamburg from circa 2015 to 2021 under the supervision of Harunaga Isaacson.

Shaoyong Ye specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies under Qing Duan at Peking University (~2003–2009) and served as an associate professor there from circa 2009 to 2011.

Sharon J. Roe is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. She completed her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies by 2014 under doctoral supervisor Steven D. Goodman and committee member James Ryan.

Sharon Salzberg is a Buddhist and religious studies practitioner and author who studied at the University at Buffalo (~1969–1971) and trained under traditional teacher Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche (~1984–1996).

Shashibhusan Dasgupta (1911–1964) was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta, where he later served as a lecturer (~1945–1964).

Shayne Clarke, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, earned an MA at the University of Canterbury and a PhD at UCLA. He held posts at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and McMaster University (~2008).

Shek-wing Tam (1935–2024) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Dudjom Rinpoche (~1972–1987) and held a post at Renmin University of China around 2007.

Sheldon Pollock is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harvard (~1971–1975). He held posts at the University of Iowa (~1980–1989), University of Chicago (1990), Clay Sanskrit Library (~2005–2008), and Columbia University (~2005–2022).
